previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a male with a history of dilated cardiomyopathy (EF 20%), type 2 diabetes, chronic kidney disease, and coronary artery disease, was admitted for chest heaviness, cough, and worsening lower extremity edema due to acute on chronic systolic heart failure. He had missed doses of clopidogrel, and labs showed elevated troponin and BNP, though EKG showed no acute changes. Mild pulmonary edema was seen on chest X-ray. He was treated with IV and oral furosemide, with improvement in symptoms and resolution of crackles. His metoprolol was reduced to 150 mg daily, and isosorbide mononitrate was increased to 60 mg. He remained on home medications including clopidogrel, aspirin, atorvastatin, and insulin. A visiting nurse was arranged to assist with medication compliance. He was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to monitor weight, follow a low-salt diet, and attend cardiology follow-up.
